title: नेपाली उपन्यासमा रचना–प्रक्रियाको विषयकरण (Thematization of composition-process in Nepali)
nepali: उपन्यास लेखनका क्रममा गरिने समग्र क्रियाकलापहरूरचना–प्रक्रिया हुन् । परम्परागत रूपमा यसलाई उपन्यासबाहिरको सन्दर्भ वा रचना–गर्भ मानिएको भए पनि पछिल्लो समय यस प्रक्रियालाई नै विषय बनाएर उपन्यास रचना भएका छन् । यस समयमा उपन्यासकारमा उपन्यास सृजनाको मानसिकता निर्माण भएको प्रसङ्गसहित लेखन र प्रकाशनसम्मका समग्र प्रक्रियालाई नै विषय बनाएर लेख्ने प्रवृत्ति देखापरिरहेको छ । यसलाई उत्तरआधुनिकतावादी आख्यानको एउटा विशेषता मानिन्छ । रचना–प्रक्रियाको विषयकरणले आख्यानबाहिरको यथार्थलाई आख्यानभित्रको काल्पनिक संसारमा प्रस्तुत गरी यथार्थ र कल्पनाबिचको भेद मेटाउँछ तर यसबाट पाठकमा एक प्रकारको भ्रम सिर्जना हुन्छ, जसलाई उत्तरआधुनितावादले यथार्थका रूपमा स्वीकार गर्दछ । यसले परम्परागत औपन्यासिक संरचनालाई भञ्जन गरी नवीन आख्यान संरचना निर्माण गर्दछ ।नेपालीमा रचना गरिएका यस प्रवृत्तिका उपन्यासहरूको खोजी र गहन अध्ययन हुन सकेको छैन । यस सन्दर्भमा रचना–प्रक्रियाको विषयकरणको सैद्धान्तिक आधार के–कस्तो रहेको छ र नेपाली उपन्यासमा रचना–प्रक्रियाको अनुकरण कसरी गरिएको छ भन्ने समस्यामा केन्द्रित भएर यो अनुसन्धान गरिएको छ ।यसका लागि उपन्यासको विषयसम्बन्धी सैद्धान्तिक मान्यताका आधारमा नेपाली उपन्यासको अध्ययन गरी रचना–प्रक्रियालाई विषयकरण गरिएका उपन्यासहरूको खोजी गरिएको छ ।ध्रुवचन्द्र गौतम र ध्रुव सापकोटाको ‘ज्यागा’(२०५०), राजेन्द्र पराजुलीको ‘अनायिका’(२०६३), टङ्कप्रसाद चौलागाईंको ‘कथाको खोजी’ (२०६४) र राजवको ‘बेकारीमा उपन्यास’(२०६९) आदि उपन्यासमा रचना–प्रक्रियाको विषयकरण गरिएको छ । यस प्रकारकाउपन्यासले नवीन विषयको खोजी गरी उपन्यासलाई काल्पनिक संसारबाट वास्तविक जीवनको यथार्थ संसारमा ल्याउने प्रयास गरेको छ । यसको परिणामस्वरूप यथार्थ र कल्पनाको भेद समाप्त भई भ्रम सिर्जना भएको छ । यस्तो लेखन उत्तरआधुनिकतावादी चिन्तनबाट प्रभावित भएकाले यसले उपन्यासको परम्परागत विधागत संरचना तथा अवधारणालाई भञ्जन गरी नवीन संरचना निर्माण पनि गरेको छ ।यसले नेपाली उपन्यासलाई प्रयोगको एउटा नयाँ मोडमा पु¥याएको भए पनि उपन्यास विधालाई जीवन र समाजको यथार्थबाट बिमुख गराएको छ ।
american_english: The overall activities carried out in the course of novel writing are the composition process. Although traditionally this has been regarded as a context outside the novel or as the womb of composition, in recent times novels have been written by making this process itself the subject. At this time a tendency is appearing to write by making the entire process, from the construction of the mentality of novel creation in the novelist to writing and publication, the subject. This is regarded as a characteristic of postmodernist narrative. The thematization of the composition process presents the reality outside the narrative in the fictional world inside the narrative, erasing the difference between reality and imagination, but this creates a kind of illusion in the reader, which postmodernism accepts as reality. It breaks the traditional novelistic structure and constructs a new narrative structure. Novels created in Nepali in this tendency have not been searched for and studied in depth. In this context, this research has been conducted, centered on the problem of what kind the theoretical basis of the thematization of the composition process is and how the imitation of the composition process has been done in the Nepali novel. For this, by studying the Nepali novel on the basis of theoretical assumptions related to the subject of the novel, a search has been made for novels in which the composition process has been thematized. In novels such as Dhruvachandra Gautam and Dhruva Sapkota's 'Jyaga' (2050), Rajendra Parajuli's 'Anayika' (2063), Tankaprasad Chaulagain's 'Kathako Khoji' (2064) and Rajav's 'Bekarima Upanyas' (2069), the composition process has been thematized. Novels of this kind have tried to bring the novel from the fictional world into the real world of actual life by searching for a new subject. As a result, the difference between reality and imagination has been eliminated and an illusion has been created. Because such writing has been influenced by postmodernist thought, it has also broken the traditional generic structure and concept of the novel and constructed a new structure. Although it has brought the Nepali novel to a new mode of experimentation, it has alienated the novel genre from the reality of life and society.

informal_english: The whole lot of activities that go into writing a novel make up the composition process. Traditionally this was seen as something outside the novel, or as the womb of composition, but lately novels have been written by making this process itself the subject. There's a trend now of writing by making the whole process the subject — from the novelist building up the mindset for creating a novel right through to writing and publication. This gets treated as a feature of postmodernist narrative. Thematizing the composition process brings the reality outside the narrative into the fictional world inside it, blurring the line between reality and imagination, but it also creates a kind of illusion in the reader, which postmodernism is happy to accept as reality. It smashes the traditional novelistic structure and builds a new narrative structure. Novels written in Nepali along these lines haven't really been dug up and studied in depth. So this research zeroes in on what the theoretical basis of thematizing the composition process actually is and how the composition process has been imitated in the Nepali novel. To do that, the Nepali novel has been studied on the basis of theoretical assumptions about the subject of the novel, and a search has been made for novels where the composition process has been thematized. In novels like Dhruvachandra Gautam and Dhruva Sapkota's 'Jyaga' (2050), Rajendra Parajuli's 'Anayika' (2063), Tankaprasad Chaulagain's 'Kathako Khoji' (2064) and Rajav's 'Bekarima Upanyas' (2069), the composition process has been thematized. Novels of this kind try to drag the novel out of the fictional world and into the real world of actual life by hunting for a new subject. The upshot is that the difference between reality and imagination gets wiped out and an illusion is created. Because this kind of writing has been shaped by postmodernist thought, it also breaks the traditional genre structure and concept of the novel and builds a new structure. So while it's pushed the Nepali novel into a new experimental mode, it's also cut the novel genre off from the reality of life and society.
